title: Compare two feature sets
description: Course activity for Exercise 2: configure two linear-regression models that predict age at scan from FreeSurfer brain morphometry, changing the measurement type and the anatomical ROI bundle, and compare their cross-validated performance side by side on one fixed cohort and one fixed set of folds.
instructions: Set a measurement type and an ROI bundle for Model A and for Model B. Each panel shows observed vs out-of-fold predicted age with a perfect-prediction diagonal, the cross-validated R-squared and MSE, and the feature count. The cohort and the folds are identical for every configuration, so any difference you see is a real difference between the feature sets.
literatureNote: Cortical structure changes with age across most of the brain rather than in one circumscribed system: large multi-site lifespan mapping (Bethlehem et al., 2022, doi:10.1038/s41586-022-04554-y) and longitudinal work on adult cortical change (Storsve et al., 2014, doi:10.1523/JNEUROSCI.0391-14.2014) both describe widespread, region-varying change with age. So, unlike a theory that predicts where to look first for IQ, there is no single small region set the age literature prefers here. The bundles below -- including 'Frontoparietal', originally assembled from IQ literature for a different activity -- are used simply as several differently sized, differently located anatomical comparisons for age.
selectionBiasNote: Trying many configurations here is exploratory model comparison. If you pick the best-looking one and report its cross-validated R-squared as the model's performance, that number is optimistic: you chose it because it looked good on this very data. An honest final estimate needs a locked-away test set or a nested procedure.
reflectionPrompts: Hold the ROI bundle fixed and change only the measurement type. Then hold the measurement type fixed and change only the bundle. Which control moves R-squared more?
Set one model to 'All eligible ROIs'. What happens to the feature count and to R-squared? Is that the same direction of change you would expect for a barely-predictable target like FIQ?
Find the single best-scoring configuration you can. Would you trust its R-squared as your final reported number for this exercise? Why or why not?
